statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013, GHSA-q4h4-gmj2-qvw2): byte arithmetic in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh can underflow and panic, fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q4h4-gmj2-qvw2). Inspected every published build of the alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 through 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), on both x86_64 and aarch64, 72 packages, each verified against the repository index checksum. The payload of every package is two files, usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool: statically linked Go programs (no ELF interpreter) built for GOOS=linux with CGO_ENABLED=0. The function names the Go linker records in each binary (its function-name table) were searched, leaving out the standard library's own copies under vendor/golang.org/x/. golang.org/x/crypto is listed in the Go build information of both programs (v0.47.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.50.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.52.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, then v0.53.0 rising to v0.58.0 by 0.34.1-r2), but the only golang.org/x/crypto packages compiled into any build are bcrypt and blowfish in alertmanager and bcrypt in amtool. No build contains any function from golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, so none of the advisory's vulnerable symbols (Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn, the Client and Server methods of the curve25519sha256, dhGEXSHA, dhGroup, ecdh and mlkem768WithCurve25519sha256 key exchanges, gcmCipher.readCipherPacket) is present. Positive control: the same search finds runtime.main and golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt functions in every binary, and finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.NewServerConn, ssh.Dial in a stripped test program built for linux/amd64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.

CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013): An incorrectly placed cast from bytes to int allowed for server-side panic in the AES-GCM packet decoder for well-crafted inputs. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://go.dev/issue/79561, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI, https://go.dev/cl/781620). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, x86_64 and aarch64), together with the doc and oci-config subpackages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Alpine security repository for Alpine 3.23 hold only an image configuration YAML file and no program. The same byte search of the same files finds the string golang.org/x/net/html, an example import path in the help text of go list, in the go command of every published golang-1.26 and golang-1.26-dev package, so the search works on these files. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013): in the AES-GCM packet decoder of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh (gcmCipher.readCipherPacket), a padding-length check adds 1 to a byte before converting it to int, so a crafted packet can wrap the value, pass the check and cause a panic. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto 0.52.0 by commit abbc44d451a6 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://go.dev/issue/79561, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/abbc44d451a6f9236a2bbd26cbcd4d0fec473da3). We read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against its index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program. The function entries in its symbol table (go tool nm) include 12 of the 14 functions the advisory lists, among them gcmCipher.readCipherPacket and NewClientConn, in all 76 binaries, so the vulnerable code is present and the status follows the module version. Builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r3 embed golang.org/x/crypto 0.48.0 to 0.51.0, which are affected. Builds 0.70.0-r4 to 0.74.0-r12 embed golang.org/x/crypto 0.52.0 to 0.59.0, which carry the fix.

Builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r3 embed golang.org/x/crypto 0.48.0 to 0.51.0, which are affected. Builds 0.70.0-r4 to 0.74.0-r12 embed golang.org/x/crypto 0.52.0 to 0.59.0, which carry the fix.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013): An incorrectly placed cast from bytes to int allowed for server-side panic in the AES-GCM packet decoder for well-crafted inputs. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://go.dev/issue/79561, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI, https://go.dev/cl/781620). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Debian security repository for Debian 13 hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog, and no program. The same byte search of the same files finds the string golang.org/x/net/html, an example import path in the help text of go list, in the go command of every published golang-1.26 and golang-1.26-dev package, so the search works on these files. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
